key_insight: This neurodegeneration biomarker study—not an AI cancer drug discovery study—developed population-based equations to express blood biomarker concentrations as individualized percentiles and Z-scores.
clinical_relevance: Accounting for age, sex, body-mass index, and renal function may improve biomarker interpretation while preserving disease-associated patterns.
method: Analyzed plasma from cognitively unimpaired participants in two French population-based cohorts.
Modeled NfL, GFAP, p-tau181, amyloid-β40, amyloid-β42, and ratios using generalized additive models.
Developed NfL cross-calibration equations across analytical methods and sample matrices.
evidence_signal: Reference populations included 5,123 participants for amyloid biomarkers and p-tau181 and 5,122 for NfL and GFAP; NfL cross-calibration achieved intraclass correlation coefficients above 0.90.
watch_item: Generalizability beyond the French reference cohorts and diagnostic utility require further validation; Z-scores alone do not establish a diagnosis.
paper_title: Population-based reference equations and Z-scores for blood biomarkers of neurodegenerative diseases
